title: MER-DG: Modality-Entropy Regularization for Multimodal Domain Generalization
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Joint fusion training makes encoders latch onto source-specific cross-modal co-occurrences that break under domain shift, causing wrong predictions.
layout: 3 panels: large left training panel, right stacked test panels; color-coded backgrounds
description: Three rounded panels show a video+audio fusion pipeline. Panel (a), gray and on the left, is source domain training. A cooking video clip and an audio waveform go into orange Video and blue Audio Encoders. Each encoder outputs green squares (domain-invariant features) and purple trapezoids (source-specific cross-modal features). A red arrow marks the purple features as complementary, and small density curves with blue arrows show the weighting toward them. Both streams feed a yellow Fusion Module. A legend sits at bottom left. Panel (b), light blue and top right, is source domain testing. The purple pieces fit together, and the output 'Cutting' gets a green check. Panel (c), light red and bottom right, is target domain testing. The input is a different kitchen scene, the purple pieces are misaligned, and the output 'Washing' gets a red X. The eye goes first to the colored encoders and the contrast between the blue and red panels.
caption: Fusion Overfitting in multimodal domain generalization. (a) During source domain training, the fusion objective causes encoders to weight their representations toward source-specific cross-modal features (purple) that complement each other, while domain-invariant features (green) remain underutilized. (b) In source domain testing, the learned cross-modal features align correctly, enabling accurate prediction. (c) In target domain testing, different recording conditions disrupt the learned co-occurrences. The cross-modal features no longer align, causing incorrect predictions.
abstract: Deploying multimodal models in real-world scenarios requires generalization to new environments where recording conditions differ from training, a challenge known as multimodal domain generalization (MMDG). Standard architectures employ separate encoders for each modality and a fusion module, training the system end-to-end by optimizing on the fused features. In this paper, we identify that such joint optimization causes encoders to exploit cross-modal co-occurrences, statistical relationships between modalities that arise from source-specific recording conditions, rather than learning domain-invariant features. We term this failure mode Fusion Overfitting. To address this, we propose Modality-Entropy Regularization for Domain Generalization (MER-DG), which maximizes the entropy of each encoder's feature distribution to preserve feature diversity. MER-DG is architecture-agnostic and integrates into existing multimodal frameworks as an additive loss term. Extensive experiments on EPIC-Kitchens and HAC benchmarks demonstrate average improvements of approximately 5% over standard fusion and approximately 2% over state-of-the-art methods.
